key_insight: With a fixed measurement basis, repetition-code process tomography needs only 0, 1 and 5 recovery gates for 3, 5 and 7 qubits, respectively—far fewer than standard decoders.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing recovery can reduce gate overhead and improve precision, but channel conditioning—not gate count—limits larger-code feasibility.
method: Exhaustively enumerate recovery designs for 3-, 5- and 7-qubit repetition codes.
Determine rank using exact modular arithmetic at two primes.
Separate how many sites to correct from which sites to correct.
evidence_signal: Across 40 sampled working points under a calibration-residual floor, a three-gate design was more precise than the standard six-gate decoder at every point, with a median improvement of 9.5×.
watch_item: The projected 10 mrad rms error in 65 seconds requires a well-conditioned three-qubit working point; codes with at least five qubits remain impractical under the studied conditioning constraints.
paper_title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
